name: snapshot-seq-aligned

graded_by.test: owed by the E2 core plan

description: The one persisted value (C6 decision 2; 5.39: counters = one, aligned). The core's commit point — recording_last_seq_out and recording_committed_offset — advances only when a grid snapshot is persisted, in the same bbolt write as the grid_snapshot_record, so at every write snapshot_seq equals recording_last_seq_out. out_bytes_committed and recording_last_seq_in are written with it, for the same point. The recording is never cut back to it (open_decisions §5): before every C3 hello the core realigns, storing a snapshot of a grid that has applied every output frame the recording holds (at a restart, the snapshot restored and the recording's own frames past the commit point re-fed), so hello carries last_committed_seq = snapshot_seq and the worker replays only what the recording lacks. A session with no grid_snapshot_record commits record-only instead, and so does one whose snapshot was not given within snapshot.wait_sec, its record deleted. The instance carries both numbers, so a core that committed a gap but had no snapshot would write two counters that can drift.

recording.warning_text: This session is recorded byte-perfect. Anything typed will be stored as-is.

instances.note: one persisted value: snapshot_seq equals recording_last_seq_out in the same write; the session carries only that one counter
